title: 36th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The 36th sitting opened with 50 members present. The chair noted that the GST amendment bill is already with the Committee of the Whole House, then the preliminary debate began on the government's bill amending the Tourism Act (Law 99/2), which raises the green tax from $6 to $12 for resorts and from $3 to $6 for guesthouses and safari boats and changes lease rules. Government-side members mostly backed it and some asked for industry consultation; MDP members opposed it, citing government borrowing, spending and the impact on tourism. Debate was still going on when this part ended. The debate on the government's bill to raise taxes on the tourism sector (an amendment to the Tourism Act, Law 2/99) continued and ended, with government-side members saying more revenue is needed after the previous government's borrowing and MDP members saying it would hurt people and tourism. After the midday recess the sponsor made closing remarks on a second government bill raising the tax and fee charged to departing airport passengers (Law 29/2016). Both bills were accepted by 58 votes to 10 and sent to a committee of the whole House for detailed study. The opening speech of this part continues from part 1, so its speaker is not named here.

items.title: Items for voting
items.outcome: both bills accepted for committee study 58-10; next sitting Monday 21 October 2024, 09:00

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Backed the bill as improving state finances and the environment, and urged quick committee review to refine it.
Said the changes are forced by the previous government's loans and mortgaged assets, and that the increases are modest.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Argued the bill is needed, saying past loans and asset handouts hurt the economy, and that tourist-borne taxes spare ordinary citizens.
As a guesthouse owner he admitted business worries but supported higher tax, citing Sri Lanka's collapse and the need for a functioning tax system.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Did not support the bill, saying government gave no explanation and that tax rises may cut arrivals and benefit neighbouring countries.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Opposed the bill, saying it raises taxes rather than widening the base, and criticised government spending and transparency on revenue.
Said the tax takes money from people's pockets and blamed government policy for the loss of the Indian tourist market; urged action on the Israeli passport ban bill.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill, saying it raises state revenue and that opposition concerns reflect their own record on income.
Said some members spread false information about the tourism slump, accused the MDP of past tourism boycott campaigns, and called Dubai and Singapore comparisons inappropriate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the bill; argued upcoming loan repayments require revenue and that the previous administration left the state in a weak financial position.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Thanked the sponsor, supported the amendment and said revenue must rise because of the previous government's debts and the state of the economy.
Said the bill's aim is debt sustainability and more foreign income, and blamed the MDP for past harm to tourism.

speakers.name: Musthafa Hussain
positions: Presented the bill: develop tourism sustainably, raise green tax to $12 resorts and $6 guesthouses, adjust lease rules, with estimated extra revenue each year to 2027.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Supported the changes made with industry consent and called for stakeholder consultation; said guesthouse operators welcome them, though he noted the sudden jump in guesthouse fees.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the bill, arguing more revenue is needed and that previous heavy borrowing and loss of funds leave little alternative to higher taxes.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said tax changes should follow consultation with the tourism industry and expressed support, while remarking that the fee rise for guesthouses is steep.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Opposed the bill; argued the government should cut spending rather than raise taxes, and criticised its borrowing and handling of public finances.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the amendment, arguing tourists, not residents, pay the tax and that revenue must be sought from lost state funds too.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill, saying the extra revenue helps government finances; welcomed lease-rule changes and an exemption for young children.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Welcomed the bill and the lease-rule publication requirement but questioned how the stay-length rule and the date of effect are set.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said his party supports the green tax change but urged consulting tourism stakeholders, and voiced guesthouse owners' concerns about financing.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Supported the bill, saying taxing tourists funds loan repayment, and backed lease provisions that return resort assets to the state.

speakers.name: Ahmed Siyam Mohamed
positions: Argued Maldives already taxes heavily compared with other destinations; said spending cuts and stopping losses at state firms matter more than higher taxes.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Opposed the bill, saying the guesthouse fee rise is large and that sudden tax increases without consultation harm businesses and local staff.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Backed the tourism tax amendment as revenue the country needs, and defended the president's wider spending cuts and health-related taxes such as on cigarettes and vapes.

speakers.name: Asadhulla Shihab
positions: As bill sponsor, said the departure fee falls on foreign passengers and funds the airport and Sovereign Development Fund; economy fares for ordinary Maldivians would not be raised.

decisions: Chair announced that the GST amendment bill is already before the Committee of the Whole House, from the 35th sitting.
Chair announced that the Tourism Act amendment bill goes to the Committee of the Whole House if the Majlis accepts it at preliminary debate.
Preliminary debate on the Tourism Act (99/2) amendment bill began and was unfinished at the end of this part.
Preliminary debate on the Tourism Act (Law 2/99) amendment bill ended after no further members asked to speak.
Tourism Act (Law 2/99) amendment bill accepted 58-10 and sent to a committee of the whole House under Rule 106(r).
Airport departing-passenger tax and fee (Law 29/2016) amendment bill accepted 58-10 and sent to a committee of the whole House under Rule 106(r).
Chair announced the next sitting for Monday 21 October 2024 at 09:00.

votes.what: Accepting the bill to amend the Tourism Act (Law 2/99)
Accepting the bill to amend the Law 29/2016 on tax and fees charged to passengers departing by airport
